advances:
The declared unique-support-vertex pentagon cell is empty.  In fact, the
contradiction uses only convexity, the two exact cap ratios, the coordinate
sign cell, and \(P\subseteq\{x+y\leq\delta\}\).  It does not use a support
segment, rationality, or the pentagon combinatorics.
author: r101_phase_support_vertex
proof:
Write
\[
M_x=\max_{p\in P}x(p),\qquad M_y=\max_{p\in P}y(p).
\tag{4}
\]
The two specified negative-coordinate points give
\(d_x\geq a>0\) and \(d_y\geq b>0\).  Since
\(P\subseteq\{x+y\leq\delta\}\),
\[
M_x\leq\delta+d_y,\qquad M_y\leq\delta+d_x.
\tag{5}
\]

Let \(v_x\in P\) have \(x(v_x)=-d_x\), and put
\[
\lambda_x=\frac{d_x}{d_x+M_x}.
\tag{6}
\]
Here \(0<\lambda_x<1\), since \(r\in P\) has positive \(x\)-coordinate.
Convexity gives
\[
v_x+\lambda_x(P-v_x)\subseteq P.
\tag{7}
\]
For every \(p\in P\), the \(x\)-coordinate of the corresponding point in
(7) is
\[
-d_x+\lambda_x(x(p)+d_x)
\leq-d_x+\lambda_x(M_x+d_x)=0.
\tag{8}
\]
Hence the homothetic copy in (7) lies in \(P\cap\{x\leq0\}\).  Area scales
by \(\lambda_x^2\), so (2) implies
\[
\frac{s}{8}\geq\lambda_x^2|P|
=16s\left(\frac{d_x}{d_x+M_x}\right)^2.
\tag{9}
\]
After cancelling \(s>0\),
\[
(d_x+M_x)^2\geq128d_x^2.
\tag{10}
\]
If \(M_x\leq10d_x\), then the left side of (10) is at most
\(121d_x^2<128d_x^2\), a contradiction.  Therefore
\[
M_x>10d_x.
\tag{11}
\]

The same argument from a point \(v_y\in P\) with \(y(v_y)=-d_y\), using
\(\lambda_y=d_y/(d_y+M_y)\), gives
\[
\frac{s}{5}\geq16s\left(\frac{d_y}{d_y+M_y}\right)^2,
\qquad
(d_y+M_y)^2\geq80d_y^2.
\tag{12}
\]
If \(M_y\leq7d_y\), the last left side is at most
\(64d_y^2<80d_y^2\).  Thus
\[
M_y>7d_y.
\tag{13}
\]

Suppose for contradiction that \(\delta<d_x+d_y\).  Combining (5), (11),
and (13) gives
\[
10d_x<M_x\leq\delta+d_y<d_x+2d_y,
\qquad
7d_y<M_y\leq\delta+d_x<2d_x+d_y.
\tag{14}
\]
The two chains in (14) imply
\[
9d_x<2d_y,\qquad 3d_y<d_x.
\tag{15}
\]
The second inequality in (15) yields \(27d_y<9d_x\), while the first yields
\(9d_x<2d_y\), contradicting \(d_y>0\).  Hence
\(\delta\geq d_x+d_y\).  Since \(d_x\geq a\) and \(d_y\geq b\), (3)
follows.

For the pentagon in the subgoal, the two specified vertices supply the
negative-coordinate points, and its unique \(x+y\)-support vertex supplies
the support hypotheses.  Thus the contradiction covers every
strict-convexity and vertex-order choice in the declared support-vertex sign
cell.  No statement or proof from the support-segment branch is used.
statement:
Let \(s,a,b,\delta>0\), and let \(P\) be a convex body contained in
\(\{x+y\leq\delta\}\).  Suppose \(P\) contains
\(r=(u,\delta-u)\) for some \(0<u<\delta\), a point with
\(x=-a\), and a point with \(y=-b\).  Put
\[
d_x=-\min_{p\in P}x(p),\qquad
d_y=-\min_{p\in P}y(p).
\tag{1}
\]
If
\[
|P|=16s,\qquad
|P\cap\{x\leq0\}|=\frac{s}{8},\qquad
|P\cap\{y\leq0\}|=\frac{s}{5},
\tag{2}
\]
then
\[
\delta\geq d_x+d_y\geq a+b.
\tag{3}
\]
Consequently, no strictly convex rational pentagon in the declared sign
cell, including one whose \(x+y\)-support face is the unique vertex
\(r=(u,\delta-u)\) with \(0<u<\delta\), satisfies (2) and
\(\delta<a+b\).
